notes:
I couldn't write these notes. My search and fetch tools stopped working at the very first request, before any page loaded. The first attempt, which tried to open six sources at once (Enduring Word, Precept Austin, NET Bible notes, and Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub), came back with the error "no more code_execution tool calls remaining this turn". A retry got the same error. My other tool has no internet access, so I had no other way to reach the approved sites.

Because your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and give a URL for every point, I haven't written any verse notes. Anything I wrote now would come from my own memory, with no real page behind the links.

**When the tools work again, I plan to:**

1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and others on BibleHub or StudyLight.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:**
   - **v. 5, being known and set apart before birth:** what it says about election and predestination, from Reformed writers (Ligonier, Desiring God, Monergism) and Wesleyan ones (Wesley's notes, Seedbed). I'd also look at how pages use the verse in teaching about the unborn (Got Questions, Lutheran Church–Missouri Synod (LCMS)).
   - **vv. 5 and 10:** whether this kind of prophetic calling continues today, from Pentecostal and charismatic sites (Sam Storms, Pneuma Review, Assemblies of God) and from the opposing view on GTY.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible translator notes (on the almond tree and "watching" wordplay in vv. 11–12, and on the north in vv. 13–15). New Advent and Catholic.com, mainly on the Church Fathers' reading of v. 5 as Jeremiah being made holy in the womb. Bible Odyssey on the opening verses (vv. 1–3) and when Jeremiah lived. Any discussion of "speaking the word" teaching linked to vv. 9 and 12.

Please send the request again in a new message and I'll start with those sources.
